work.name: University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
work.summary: Developed CliPP-on-Web to bring subclonal reconstruction to clinicians and quantified compartment-specific plasticity. Mined pre- and post-treatment SNV/CNV profiles from clinical trials to detect emerging resistance, monitor disease trajectory, and link signals to outcomes (response, PFS/OS) and biomarker signatures.

projects.name: Subclonal Reconstruction to Predict Immunotherapy Response
projects.summary: Computed subclonal mutational load (sML) via subclonal reconstruction and showed that high sML predicts improved survival and response to immune checkpoint blockade, particularly in cancers with low-to-moderate TMB. Integrated Cox models and pan-cancer validations; packaged methods for prospective use.
highlights: sML metric from subclonal reconstruction pipelines
Association with ICB response and survival
Stratification beyond TMB in low/moderate-TMB tumors

projects.name: Ultra-Deep Sequencing for Sensitive Variant Detection
projects.summary: Established error profiles for SNVs vs. Indels vs. SVs under ultra-deep sequencing to enable sensitive detection (e.g., MRD). Found Indel/SV error rates orders of magnitude lower than SNVs overall, with repeat-Indels as key failure modes—informing marker selection, assay design, and statistical thresholds for rare-variant calling.
highlights: MRD assay: NGS outperforms flow cytometry at higher burdens

projects.name: Oncogenic Fusions in Pediatric Cancers
projects.summary: Comprehensive discovery and mechanistic modeling of oncogenic gene fusions across 5,190 childhood cancers. Built a fusion-calling and curation pipeline, characterized four etiologic categories (neo-translational, intronic versioning, neo-splicing, chimeric exon), and linked specific fusion architectures to clinical outcomes and therapeutic vulnerabilities (e.g., neo-splice-site targets).
highlights: Multi-caller RNA-seq fusion detection (Arriba, STAR-Fusion, CICERO, FusionCatcher)

projects.name: Soccer Player Detection & Tracking in Video
projects.summary: This project develops and evaluates a system for automatically detecting and tracking soccer players in match video footage. The goal is to robustly handle challenges like occlusion, scale variation, different camera views, and varying lighting, to produce continuous, accurate tracks of players over time.
highlights: Player detection in broadcast soccer video under occlusion
Data association and multi-object tracking for players
Use of field calibration or multi-view geometry when available
Handling scale changes, motion, and appearance similarity across players

projects.name: Reality-Based Interaction Framework
projects.summary: This project investigates the Reality-Based Interaction (RBI) framework, which proposes that interaction modalities closer to people's everyday reality (e.g. physical manipulation, body awareness, environmental awareness) can improve human-computer interfaces. The work defines different dimensions of Reality-Based Interaction and provides design implications for building systems using more 'real' interaction modes.
